title: Total budget for the year
context: The Ledger (rows 2-97) has one line per department per month. Finance needs the headline budget figure.
task: What is the total amount budgeted across every line in the ledger?
hint: Find the column holding the budgeted amount and add it all up.

title: Total actual spend
context: One ledger line has no actual recorded yet.
task: How much did the company actually spend in total across the whole year?
hint: Total the actual-spend column; the blank line is simply skipped.

title: Variance on one line
context: Variance is how far actual spend landed from what was budgeted.
task: By how much did the line in row 2 come in over or under budget? (Positive means it spent more than planned.)
hint: Subtract the budgeted amount from the actual amount for that row.

title: Variance as a percentage
context: Reviewers prefer to see overspend relative to the budget, not in raw currency.
task: Express row 2's variance as a percentage of its budget, shown like "12.5%".
hint: Divide the row's variance by its budget, then format the result as a percentage string.

title: Company-wide variance
context: The CFO wants the bottom-line gap between spend and plan.
task: Across the whole year, how much more (or less) did the company spend than it budgeted?
hint: Take the total of actuals and subtract the total of budgets.

title: Lines over budget
context: Each ledger line has both a budget and an actual sitting side by side.
task: On how many ledger lines did actual spend come in above the budget?
hint: You need to compare the two columns row by row and tally the wins; SUMPRODUCT of a comparison does this.

title: Capital expenditure lines
context: Each line is tagged as either Capex or Opex.
task: How many ledger lines are classed as capital expenditure (Capex)?
hint: Count the rows whose type equals Capex.

title: Engineering's budget
context: The Engineering lead wants their allocated budget.
task: What is the total budget allocated to the Engineering department?
hint: Sum the budget column, but only for rows where the department is Engineering.

title: Engineering's actual spend
context: Now compare that budget against what Engineering really spent.
task: How much did the Engineering department actually spend over the year?
hint: Sum the actual column for rows where the department is Engineering.

title: Capital spend total
context: Finance separates capital spend from operating spend.
task: What was the total actual spend on lines tagged as Capex?
hint: Sum actuals, filtered to rows whose type is Capex.

title: Average budget per line
context: The dashboard shows a clean whole-number figure.
task: What is the average budget across all ledger lines, rounded to a whole number?
hint: Average the budget column, then round the result to zero decimals.

title: Typical Sales spend
context: How much does Sales spend in a typical month?
task: What is the average monthly actual spend for the Sales department?
hint: Average the actual column, restricted to Sales rows.

title: Biggest spend line
context: Finance wants to spot the single heaviest charge.
task: What is the largest actual spend on any single ledger line?
hint: Find the maximum in the actual column.

title: Smallest actual value
context: One line carries a credit, which sits below zero.
task: What is the smallest actual value recorded anywhere in the ledger?
hint: Find the minimum of the actual column.

title: Over or under?
context: Each line should be flagged against its budget.
task: Label the line in row 2 as "Over" if actual exceeded budget, otherwise "Under".
hint: A single IF comparing the row's actual to its budget.

title: Material variance?
context: A variance only matters if it is large relative to budget, in either direction.
task: Flag row 2 as "Material" if its variance is more than 10% of its budget either way, otherwise "OK".
hint: Compare the size of the gap (ignore its sign) against 10% of the budget inside an IF.

title: Who owns this budget?
context: The Depts table (H2:J9) maps each department to its Owner.
task: Who is the owner of the department on the ledger line in row 2?
hint: Match the row's department into the Depts table and pull back the owner column.

title: Variance threshold
context: The Assumptions table (O2:P5) stores the model's settings by name.
task: Pull the value set for the "Variance threshold" assumption.
hint: Match the assumption label into the Assumptions table and return its value column.

title: Month of a line
context: Reporting groups the ledger by month.
task: Which month number (1-12) does the ledger line in row 2 belong to?
hint: Extract the month from the row's date.

title: Which quarter?
context: Finance reports on a quarterly cycle.
task: Which calendar quarter (like "Q1") does the line in row 5 fall in?
hint: Derive the quarter from the month number, then prefix it with "Q".

title: Month label
context: Charts want a tidy month-year caption.
task: Show the date of row 2 as a label like "Jan-2025".
hint: Format the row's date into a month-year text pattern.

title: Month-end date
context: Accruals are booked on the last day of the month.
task: Return the last calendar day of the month for the line in row 2.
hint: There is a function that jumps to the end of a month.

title: Cost-centre number
context: Cost centres are coded like "CC100"; a report needs just the digits as a number.
task: Extract the numeric part of row 2's cost-centre code as a real number (e.g. CC100 becomes 100).
hint: Pull out the digits after the two letters, then convert that text into a number.

title: Line label
context: Build a readable caption like "Engineering · Jan" for the line in row 2.
task: Join row 2's department, a " · " separator, and its month abbreviation.
hint: Stitch the department to the month name (formatted from the date) with &.

title: Budget in lakhs
context: Indian reports quote large figures in lakhs (units of 100,000).
task: Show row 2's budget in lakhs to two decimals, followed by " L".
hint: Divide the budget by 100,000, format it to two decimals as text, then append " L".

title: Missing actuals
context: A data-quality check looks for lines still awaiting an actual figure.
task: How many ledger lines are missing an actual value?
hint: Count the blank cells in the actual column.

title: Credits recorded
context: Negative actuals represent credits or reversals.
task: How many lines have a negative actual value?
hint: Count the actual column with a less-than-zero criterion.

title: Over budget and capital?
context: Finance wants to catch capital lines that also blew their budget.
task: For row 2, return TRUE only if it is over budget AND tagged as Capex.
hint: Combine two conditions that must both hold.

title: Possible data issue?
context: A line is suspicious if its actual is missing or negative.
task: For row 2, return TRUE if the actual is blank OR the actual is negative.
hint: Either condition being true is enough; one test checks for a blank cell.

title: January exchange rate
context: The FX table (columns L-M) lists the INR-per-USD rate for each month.
task: What is the INR-per-USD rate for the first month in the FX table?
hint: Point directly at the rate cell for that first month.

title: Line converted to USD
context: The actuals are in rupees; a US parent wants them in dollars.
task: Convert row 2's actual spend into USD using January's exchange rate, to 2 decimals.
hint: Divide the rupee actual by the exchange rate, then round to two places.

title: Engineering's share
context: How much of the pie does Engineering hold?
task: What percentage of the total budget belongs to Engineering, shown like "12.5%"?
hint: Divide Engineering's budget by the overall budget total, then format as a percentage.

title: Budget utilisation
context: Leadership wants a single figure for how much of budget was used.
task: Overall, what percentage of the total budget was actually spent, shown like "98.5%"?
hint: Divide total actuals by total budget, then format the ratio as a percentage.

title: How many departments?
context: The Depts table (starting column H) lists each department once.
task: How many departments are listed in the Depts table?
hint: Count the department name cells; they are text, so a plain number count won't do.
